summary: A target-level continuation completing the planning pass for the later localization comparison. It reuses the four existing local/Dedekind/transfer comparison targets and the earlier-owned Milnor residue and norm theory. Three additional targets package the pointwise finite-support residue family, compare the ordered Milnor product map with the signed Quillen boundary in every degree, and distinguish Milnor unit-part specialization from Quillen specialization by its explicit correction. The product-normalized Matsumoto map is used throughout, retaining the torus sign against the Hurewicz comparison. All scoped targets are planned, not formalized or supplier-closed; the precise torsion-Serre quotient, product-model comparison, inherited Matsumoto inputs and arbitrary-residue complete-DVR support remain recorded owner contracts.

nodes.title: The product map intertwines higher residues with the signed localization boundary
nodes.statement: Let R be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field F, residue field k and parameter π. Write r_v,n : K⁽ᴹ⁾_n(F) → K⁽ᴹ⁾_(n−1)(k) for T.3/higher-milnor-residues with the parameter LAST; Φ_n for T.2/graded-map, defined by the ordered product of unit classes; and D_n : K_n(F) → K_(n−1)(k) for the actual K.3 localization connecting map with D₁[π]=1 and the RIGHT module convention. For every n≥1, D_n ∘ Φ_n = (−1)^(n−1) Φ_(n−1) ∘ r_v,n. Thus δ_n=(−1)^(n−1)D_n satisfies δ_nΦ_n=Φ_(n−1)r_v,n. In degree two Φ₂=θ₂♮m is the product-normalized Matsumoto equivalence, and D₂Φ₂{f,g}=t_v(f,g)⁻¹, whereas δ₂Φ₂=t_v. If θ₂♮(z)=θ₂(εz) for the globally fixed torus sign ε∈{±1}, then D₂θ₂m=−εr_v,2 in additive residue notation, or t_v^(−ε) multiplicatively. No value of ε is assumed and no higher Φ_n is asserted invertible.
hypotheses: R is a commutative DVR; F is its fraction field and k its native residue field. No completeness, finite residue field, coefficient field or characteristic restriction is assumed.
K.3 supplies the torsion-module localization sequence, dévissage and resolution, and its right product boundary law. Φ₀ identifies the integer class with rank, and Φ₁ takes a unit to its K₁ class.
The comparison θ₂♮, rather than an unspecified classical-to-Quillen isomorphism, is the one fixed by T.2/graded-map-degree-two-identification.
proofSteps: Expand every symbol using f_i=u_iπ^(a_i). Bilinearity, skew-commutativity and {π,π}={−1,π} reduce it to a sum of symbols of R-units and symbols {u₁,…,u_(n−1),π}. This is an argument on generators, not a claimed splitting of Milnor K-theory of R.
A product of R-unit classes lifts to K_n(R), so its boundary is zero by localization exactness. Its reduction is Φ of the reduced units by naturality of K.7 products.

For a unit product b of degree n−1, the left action obtained from the right module law gives D_n(Φ(b)·[π])=(−1)^(n−1)Φ(b̄)D₁[π]. Dévissage sends D₁[π]=[k] to 1. This is exactly the residue value on a uniformizer-last symbol.
Agreement on all symbol generators proves equality of homomorphisms in every degree. In degree two substitute the imported product-normalized equivalence Φ₂=θ₂♮m and use ε²=1 to transport to θ₂.
For f=π^a u and g=π^b v, the resulting multiplicative value is (−1)^(ab) v̄^a ū^(−b), the inverse of the roadmap tame symbol. The diagonal π,π contributes −1, not 1.
acceptance: At ℚ with the 5-adic valuation: t₅(2,5)=2, D₂Φ₂{2,5}=3; t₅(5,2)=3, D₂Φ₂{5,2}=2; D₂Φ₂{5,5}=4 in 𝔽₅ˣ. These distinguish inversion from the identity.

D₁Φ₁{π}=1. For k=ℚ(t), R=k[[π]] and x={2,t,π}, D₃Φ₃(x)=Φ₂{2,t}. The t-adic boundary of the right side is 1/2∈ℚˣ, while that of its negative is 2. This detects the positive degree-three sign; a finite-field K₂ target cannot do so.
All-unit symbols have zero boundary. δ₂ and D₂ have the same kernel and inverse values, but their map equality is never asserted.
Transport through θ₂ carries ε explicitly. A finite-field K₂=0 test cannot determine that sign.

sources.locator: III.7.3, printed p.246 / PDF p.254; V.6.6.1, printed p.409 / PDF p.417; Exercise V.5.3, printed p.405 / PDF p.413

nodes.title: Package the finite-support family as a total Milnor residue homomorphism
nodes.statement: Let V be an indexed family of normalized discrete valuations on a field F of finite character: for each a∈Fˣ only finitely many v∈V have ord_v(a)≠0. For n≥1 construct MilnorK.globalResidueHom(V,n) : K⁽ᴹ⁾_n(F) → ⨁_(v∈V) K⁽ᴹ⁾_(n−1)(k_v), the unique additive homomorphism with v-coordinate r_v,n. The direct sum is the existing dependent DirectSum, using Additive k_vˣ in degree one. It is not the direct sum of the individual homomorphisms: each input has finite support, while infinitely many component homomorphisms may be nonzero. For a Dedekind domain R with F=Frac(R) and V its nonzero primes, the total Quillen boundary satisfies D⁽ᴿ⁾_n Φ_n = (−1)^(n−1)(⨁_v Φ_(n−1)) globalResidueHom(V,n). In particular degree two transports the inherited Dedekind sequence through Φ₂ and coordinatewise negation/inversion.
hypotheses: n≥1, V is a set-indexed family with the explicit finite-character property, and every residue field is the native residue of its valuation ring.

The global Quillen comparison clause uses the height-one-prime family of a Dedekind domain and its actual localization sequence. No full Quillen boundary into a direct sum is postulated for an arbitrary family of DVRs.
proofSteps: Import T.3/finite-support: a finite sum of symbols has residue support inside the finite union of the order supports of all entries. Use it to construct an element of the existing dependent direct sum from the coordinate function v↦r_v,n(x).

Coordinatewise additivity and DirectSum.ext prove the homomorphism laws and uniqueness. The construction is independent of a symbol presentation because every coordinate is already a homomorphism on Milnor K-theory.

For Dedekind primes, the pinned Support.finite theorem controls poles only. Apply it to both a and a⁻¹ to bound the nonzero-order support. For function-field places import TauCeti.Place.finite_setOf_ord_ne_zero directly. No new place or divisor is defined.

For the global square compare coordinates using product-residue-comparison and the factorization of the localization boundary through R_v. DirectSum.map supplies the componentwise Φ, and DirectSum.ext assembles equality.

The inherited exact sequence retains its ordinary Quillen arrow D₂. To display the roadmap residue arrow, compose that arrow with negation on the residue direct sum and the following arrow with negation on its source. Exactness then follows from an isomorphism of sequences, not merely from equality of kernels.
acceptance: The constructor uses pointwise finite support, not a finitely supported family of maps.
In degree one the map is the existing principal-divisor coefficient map on the chosen family, and in degree two its coordinates are the roadmap t_v.
Every API item below is specified and every test below has a concrete expected value or failure. The full Quillen sequence and transfers remain imported under their existing identifiers.

sources.locator: III.6.5, printed pp.236–237 / PDF pp.244–245; III.7.4, printed pp.247–248 / PDF pp.255–256; V.6.6–6.6.1, printed p.409 / PDF p.417

api.name: MilnorK.globalResidueHom
api.statement: The additive homomorphism to the dependent residue direct sum, constructed with the finite-support proof for each input.

api.name: MilnorK.globalResidueHom_apply
api.statement: For every v and x, the v-coordinate of globalResidueHom(V,n)(x) is r_v,n(x).

api.name: MilnorK.globalResidueHom_unique
api.statement: A homomorphism to this direct sum with all the same residue coordinates equals globalResidueHom(V,n).

api.name: MilnorK.globalResidueHom_support_subset
api.statement: For any finite symbol expression for x, the support of globalResidueHom(V,n)(x) is contained in the union of the nonzero-order supports of all its entries; equality is not asserted.

api.name: MilnorK.globalResidueHom_eq_zero_iff
api.statement: globalResidueHom(V,n)(x)=0 iff r_v,n(x)=0 for every v. Thus its kernel is the intersection of the individual residue kernels.

api.name: MilnorK.globalResidueHom_degree_one
api.statement: At n=1 the coordinates are ord_v(a); for Dedekind primes and for function-field places, compare to the existing principal divisor by coefficient extensionality.

api.name: MilnorK.globalResidueHom_degree_two
api.statement: At n=2 its coordinates in k_vˣ are t_v(f,g), with addition on Additive k_vˣ interpreted multiplicatively.

api.name: MilnorK.globalResidueHom_quillen
api.statement: For a Dedekind R, D⁽ᴿ⁾_n Φ_n=(−1)^(n−1)DirectSum.map(Φ_(n−1)) globalResidueHom(V,n). This compares actual maps, not only groups.

api.name: MilnorK.globalResidueHom_reindex
api.statement: Relabeling V by an equivalence, and transporting its valuations and native residue fields along that equivalence, reindexes the output. No unrestricted field-extension naturality is claimed.

uses.how: Identifies the residue-kernel subgroup using the existing finite-support codomain, and supplies the correctly signed map from the imported Dedekind localization row.
Exports the field-symbol boundary calculation and actual direct-sum comparison for the affine Dedekind/DVR cases; scheme support and curve gluing stay with those consumers.

Provides reusable coordinate and finite-support vocabulary. Their norms, proper-curve reciprocity and place/closed-point dictionaries remain earlier-owned inputs, not prerequisites introduced by this construction.

tests.name: MilnorK.globalResidueHom_empty
tests.statement: For V empty the codomain is trivial and every input maps to zero. For x=0 all coordinates are zero for any V.

tests.name: MilnorK.globalResidueHom_principal_divisor
tests.statement: For F=ℚ and V the rational primes, globalResidueHom(V,1){25/2} has coefficient −1 at 2, coefficient 2 at 5, and zero elsewhere. These are the coefficients of the existing principal divisor of 25/2; degree zero of each residue group is ℤ, not a residue-field unit group.

tests.name: MilnorK.globalResidueHom_rational_symbol
tests.statement: For F=ℚ and V the rational primes, globalResidueHom(V,2){2,5} has only its 5-coordinate nontrivial, with value 2∈𝔽₅ˣ. The coordinate at 2 is 1 because 𝔽₂ˣ is trivial. The Quillen-boundary coordinate is 3 at 5.

tests.name: MilnorK.globalResidueHom_steinberg
tests.statement: For the same family, {2,−1}={2,1−2} maps to zero at every prime. Its entries have a nonzero-order support at 2, so the support bound can be strict.

tests.name: MilnorK.globalResidueHom_inverse_and_diagonal
tests.statement: For ℚ at the prime 5, {5,2} has coordinate 3 and {5,5} has coordinate 4. Adding a symbol to its additive inverse yields the zero direct-sum element.

tests.name: MilnorK.globalResidueHom_degree_three
tests.statement: For k=ℚ(t), F=k((π)) and V the singleton π-adic family, globalResidueHom(V,3){2,t,π} has coordinate {2,t}∈K⁽ᴹ⁾₂(k). Its image under Φ₂ has t-adic Quillen boundary 1/2∈ℚˣ. The actual D₃ has the positive coordinate Φ₂{2,t}; negating it would give t-adic boundary 2.

tests.name: MilnorK.globalResidueHom_infinite_family
tests.statement: For V=ℕ with every indexed valuation the same 5-adic valuation on ℚ, {2,5} has the nontrivial coordinate 2 at every index. Finite character fails, so this input cannot be sent to a dependent direct sum by the proposed coordinates.

nodes.title: Compare unit-part specialization with the two Quillen product specializations
nodes.statement: With R,F,k,π,Φ,D and r as in product-residue-comparison, let λ_π,n be the imported Milnor unit-part specialization and n≥1. Then λ_π,n(x)=r_v,n+1(x·{−π}) and Φ_n(λ_π,n(x))=(−1)^n D_(n+1)(Φ_n(x)·[−π]). For the K-book specialization q_π,n(z)=D_(n+1)([π]·z), one instead has q_π,n(Φ_n x)=Φ_n(λ_π,n(x)+r_v,n(x)·{−1}). Equivalently, q_π,nΦ_n=Φ_nλ_(−π),n. For π′=uπ with u∈Rˣ, both these compared specializations change by −Φ_n(r_v,n(x)·{ū}); r_v and D are independent of π. These are equalities of homomorphisms; they do not assert an all-degree isomorphism or identify q_π with λ_π.
hypotheses: n≥1; λ_π is T.3/higher-milnor-residues in the same parameter-last convention as r.
q_π uses the K-book RIGHT-linear boundary and multiplication by [π] on the LEFT. The corrected formula uses [−π] on the RIGHT and the degree sign.
proofSteps: Use the imported Serre expansion d_π(x)=λ_π(x)+r_v(x)Π, with Π on the right. Since d_π{−π}={−1}+Π, Π{−1}=−{−1}Π and Π²={−1}Π, the coefficient of Π in d_π(x)d_π{−π} is exactly λ_π(x). Thus r_v(x{−π})=λ_π(x).
Apply product-residue-comparison in degree n+1 to x{−π} and use multiplicativity of Φ. This proves the corrected Quillen formula.
For q_π commute the degree-one [π] past Φ_n(x). The factor (−1)^n from graded commutativity cancels the factor (−1)^n of the boundary comparison. The coefficient of Π in d_π(x)Π is λ_π(x)+r_v(x){−1}.

The parameter-change formula of T.3/specialisation-change-of-uniformiser gives λ_(uπ)=λ_π−r_v·{ū}. Bilinearity and the right module law give the same change for q. For u=−1 the sign of the correction is immaterial because {−1} is killed by 2, so q_πΦ=Φλ_(−π).
On unramified unit products r_v=0, both formulas reduce to reduction of units. On {π} they differ; this is a mathematical distinction between the source constructions, not a new source erratum.
acceptance: For R=ℤ_(5), λ₅,1{5}=0 in additive Milnor notation, but q₅,1([5])=[−1], corresponding to 4∈𝔽₅ˣ. The corrected expression −D₂([5]·[−5])=0.
For the same R, λ₁₀,1{5}={3}, while q₁₀,1([5])={2}, because q₅{5}−{2}={−1/2}={2} in 𝔽₅ˣ. A uniformizer-independent specialization fails this test.
For a unit u both specializations take Φ₁{u} to [ū]. In higher degree every all-unit symbol reduces in its original order.
For k=ℚ(s), F=k((t)), x={s,t}, λ_t,2(x)=0 and q_t,2Φ₂(x)=Φ₂{s,−1}; the latter is detected by the s-adic residue −1. This tests the correction beyond degree one.

sources.locator: III.7.3 and its Serre algebra proof, printed p.246 / PDF p.254; V.6.6.4 and the specialization paragraph immediately following it, printed p.410 / PDF p.418

Three new target-level nodes refine the inherited four comparison nodes; earlier Milnor residues, specialization, product signs, finite support and norm construction are imported without duplicate IDs. The reader states their exact maps, hypotheses, API and tests.

requests.need: For every Dedekind domain R with fraction field F, finitely generated torsion R-modules form a Serre subcategory of finitely generated R-modules, and localization induces an exact equivalence of the Serre quotient with finite-dimensional F-vector spaces. Retain the functorial identifications for R→R_p and for restriction of scalars along finite inclusions of Dedekind domains. Dévissage identifies the torsion term with the filtered finite-support sum of the residue-field K-theories. K.3/abelian-localization-theorem, devissage-theorem and resolution-theorem are imported named inputs, not substitutes for this quotient equivalence. Source: K-book II.6.4.1 and V.6.1, V.6.6.

Compare K.7's product with Loday's plus-construction product in degree (1,1). For rings A and A′, under the identification of the base-point component of the K-theory space with BGL(−)⁺ (K.2:plus/plus-equals-Q) and of K₁ with π₁BGL⁺ (KTheoryLowDegrees U.6/pi1-plus-construction), the degree-(1,1) part K₁(A) ⊗ K₁(A′) → K₂(A ⊗ A′) of the biexact external product of K.7/products-from-biexact-functors equals Loday's product [f]∗[f′] = [γ ∘ (f ∧ f′)] (Loday §2.1.10 and Theorem 2.1.11; Weibel IV.1.10), where γ is built from tensor products of matrices and the block-sum H-space structure. State it naturally in A and A′, with the identification S¹ ∧ S¹ ≅ S² used by K.7's sign conventions made explicit; for a commutative ring the internal product is this followed by the multiplication R ⊗ R → R. The value on two unit classes and its sign relative to T.1/k2-pi2 are planned in K2SymbolsBrauer:T.2/unit-loop-product-symbol and are not requested. K.7/products-from-biexact-functors and K.7/unit-multiplication-and-K0-tensor-comparison do not state this comparison, and the locators read here state the plus product only.
requests.inheritedFrom: K2SymbolsBrauer--T.2-graded-map; no second unit-symbol theorem is requested here.

gaps.title: Inherited classical presentation inputs
gaps.detail: The accepted T.2:symbols plan retains G-finite-classical and G-stable-witness. This continuation uses T.2/graded-map-degree-two-identification, which explicitly inherits them; no assertion that checking the Steinberg relations proves Matsumoto injectivity is made. Owner: K2SymbolsBrauer T.2:symbols. The all-degree product/residue comparison itself only needs the existing Milnor presentation and product map, not invertibility in higher degrees.

gaps.title: Inherited generic complete-DVR support for Milnor norms
gaps.detail: The general Milnor norm/residue proof used by T.4 and T.3/transfer-and-norm-residue rests on the unregistered Local Fields and Ramification, Part II routing brief in the existing T.3 packet, contracts DVR.0–DVR.3 (finite extensions, integral-closure lattice, norm valuation/residue, component lengths). The current upstream local-field roadmap assumes finite residue field and does not supply those general contracts. Preserve the earlier gap and routing brief; proposed identifiers are not executable prerequisites here. The Quillen finite-Dedekind localization/transfer square and the two-transfer equality proof by arbitrary FIELD base change do not use this complete-DVR gap.

restructure.detail: Retain RT-AREA-ktheory-1/28: T.3:symbols → T.4 → T.3:localization-comparison. Move the higher Milnor residue/specialization/product-sign and finite-support text to T.3:symbols, whose existing nodes realize this stage. Keep the later stage for comparison with Quillen K-theory. This is a maintainer change to the atlas, not an edit here.

The existing localization-boundary, dedekind-localization-boundary and milnor-quillen-transfer-comparison targets remain their single owners. Assembly must read their classical-to-Quillen identification as Φ₂=θ₂♮m from T.2/graded-map-degree-two-identification. If a consumer uses the Hurewicz θ₂ instead, retain ε and replace D₂Φ₂=−r₂ by D₂θ₂m=−εr₂. For a displayed exact row with arrow r₂ rather than D₂, also negate the following residue-to-K₁ arrow.

upstreamNotes.note: Consumer, not a prerequisite. Its ring/scheme adapter imports the product-normalized boundary formula and distinguishes actual D₂ from δ₂=−D₂. Scheme support, coherent/perfect comparison and closed-point gluing remain S.3-owned. No S.3 input is used to prove the DVR ring comparison.

Consumer, not a prerequisite. Use the same parameter-last residue convention and identify its curve maps via the scheme/place dictionary owned elsewhere. Finite pushforward uses residue norms without an extra ramification factor; pullback has the ramification factor.

The index, DVR degree-one boundary, right product boundary and arbitrary-field transfer base-change are precise existing plan nodes, not new requests or pinned declarations. The requested torsion Serre quotient remains outstanding. Artinian component lengths belong to G-theory dévissage; no K(B)=G(B) for a nonregular Artin ring is used.

Current main supplies finite-residue local-field norm valuations, and AlgebraicCurves supplies function-field places, normalization and completion interfaces. Read both current Suggested.lean files and the current Tau Ceti library. None supplies Quillen/Milnor K-theory or the full arbitrary-residue finite-extension support; preserve the inherited Part II routing brief without widening either upstream roadmap.
